principles: Do not optimize for the sake of optimization.
Keep host-neutral CLI non-authority boundaries intact.
drivers: Close exactly the two signed-workspace high gaps from gap_analyze.
Avoid adding gitRoot repair UX or Layer4/customerKeyRef work to this story.

options.name: A: Add minimal source-level coverage bindings to existing signed-workspace implementation
pros: Matches the actual gap_analyze failure mode.
Does not introduce new product behavior.
Keeps the story small and auditable.
cons: Requires precise annotation text so the scanner recognizes both requirements.

options.name: B: Change gap_analyze keyword matching logic
pros: Could make future coverage matching less brittle.
cons: Broader than the current correctness issue.
Risks changing convergence behavior for unrelated requirements.

options.name: C: Implement gitRoot repair UX now
cons: Would mix a new product feature with a coverage binding fix.
Could create additional gates and token cost.

chosen: A: Add minimal source-level coverage bindings to existing signed-workspace implementation
rationale: The code already contains the signed-workspace fail-closed behavior and regression coverage; gap_analyze is reporting uncovered requirements because the truth-source strings are not bound to source annotations. Minimal source-level binding fixes the real correctness issue without expanding scope.

preMortem.scenario: Annotation text is too generic and gap_analyze still reports the same two high gaps.
preMortem.trigger: The exact unresolved reason or no-binding diagnostic phrase is absent from title/description/changes.
preMortem.consequence: The story appears changed but does not unlock convergence for the signed-workspace requirements.
preMortem.mitigation: Include the exact requirement strings from lines 262 and 311 and verify with lattice gap_analyze before marking done.

preMortem.scenario: The fix accidentally becomes gitRoot repair UX work.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation adds config repair commands or nested repo detection instead of coverage binding.
preMortem.consequence: Scope creep increases complexity and violates user constraints.
preMortem.mitigation: Scope contract excludes repair UX/config repair and REVIEW checks changed files against the contract.

preMortem.scenario: The fix hides the customerKeyRef Layer4 gap.
preMortem.trigger: Annotation text accidentally mentions customerKeyRef as covered or analyzer logic is loosened globally.
preMortem.consequence: Layer4 capability could be falsely claimed as covered.
preMortem.mitigation: Do not touch customerKeyRef implementation or analyzer matching; require gap_analyze to still show customerKeyRef as the only remaining high gap.
